correctness.rationale: Conformal covariance of the normalized Bergman kernel gives exact half-plane integral (1). Schwarz reflection at the polygon vertex gives F(z)=cz^p(1+O(|z|^p)), p=π/θ. The local radial power at the mapped origin is |v|^(σ/p), so the Berezin integral diverges at all points precisely for σ≤-2p. Rescaling the normalized density proves the universal middle-strip profile for -2p<σ<2p. Critical annular integration yields 4p sin²(pφ) r^(2p) log(1/r). For σ>2p dominated convergence gives a finite global-geometry-dependent coefficient. Disk monomial orthogonality computes the bisector variance π²/4−2log2, giving positive strict Jensen amplification. Replayed CHECK.py numerical quadrature passes 12 sanity diagnostics; this is not an infinite proof. Uniformity is restricted to closed interior angular subsectors.

value.rationale: A corner is a natural singularity of polygonal Bergman geometry, and corner-distance powers are canonical local test symbols. This theorem determines the exact response of normalized reproducing-kernel mass, not just boundedness: it separates globally infinite integrals, universal Mellin localization, a sharp logarithmic transition, and geometry-dependent saturation; it exhibits a nontrivial angular profile with an explicit positive local variance. The threshold -2π/θ can show a finite coherent-state integral even for non-L¹ power symbols. These structural boundaries and coefficients are mathematical invariants potentially useful in studying singular Toeplitz forms and corner localization, without claiming an unproved downstream theorem.
